request.title: [Review] Independent check that the terminology revision #477 preserves the mathematics
request.body:
### Task kind
review-math

### Proposed coordinator
@hairer (maintainer); task opened by ADB991's scheduled agent session `ADB991-claude-20261116-81c1`.

### Mathematical interface and source scope
PR #477 (merged as `962ac43b`, base `9ded0b7a`) renamed terminology across 182 manuscript files (+3092/−3064 lines): price/bill/voucher-style labels became bounds or named roles, `temp`→`fieldCut`, `fiery`→`fineCut`, and so on. It also separated the grade dilation $\mathsf D^{\rm gr}_{d,L}$ from the link-product map $\mathsf D_m$ and changed the layout of a few displays. The PR states that it keeps reference keys and numerical constants, and that "the terminology changes remain open to independent editorial and mathematical review". This task is that review, limited to one question: **does the #477 diff `9ded0b7a..962ac43b` preserve the mathematics of `manuscript/existence/*.tex` and `manuscript/existence.tex`?** Lean source revision `3456e5e75cf8d4cd558955a5c7638fba2d68f464` is unaffected; `Lean/` is not touched.

Concretely:
1. **Name collisions.** Check that no new name (macro, operator name, or prose term used as a defined object) already denoted a different object before #477 in the same scope. Check that two formerly distinct names were not merged into one.
2. **Rename completeness.** Find renamed objects that still appear under the old name somewhere, and new names that are used before they are defined.
3. **Math-mode invariance.** After the rename map is applied, check that math-mode content is unchanged: constants, exponents, indices, inequalities, quantifiers. Read each display whose layout changed and confirm the two versions are equivalent.
4. **Dilation split.** Check that each use of $\mathsf D^{\rm gr}_{d,L}$ vs $\mathsf D_m$ matches the object actually meant at that point (grade and block size explicit, per the PR).
5. **Labels and references.** Check that the sets of `\label` and `\ref`/`\eqref`/`\cite` keys are unchanged, or that any change is intended.

### Expository treatment and literature search
Not applicable: this is a review of an editorial diff and introduces no new mathematics. Literature citations are checked only to confirm that #477 left them unchanged.

### Owned outputs and exclusions
Owned:
- `blueprint/units/YM-000026/reviews/terminology-477-review-ADB991-claude-20261116-81c1.md` (review report: findings, rename map, evidence)
- `Bots/notes/<this issue>-20261116T2330Z-ADB991-claude-20261116-81c1.md` (reusable rename-map and collision-check method)

Exclusions: no edits to `manuscript/`, `unit.json` status or any other reviewer's record. Fixing any finding is a separate author task. This task does not cover a whole-argument mathematical re-review, Lean correspondence, or the earlier consolidation in #471.

### Prerequisites and overlap search
Prerequisite: #477 is merged (satisfied). Overlap search on 2026-11-16 23:15 UTC: there are no open issues or PRs. #26, #62 and #472 are closed. No existing review of #477 was found in `blueprint/units/YM-000026/reviews/` or in PR comments. A concurrent ADB991 session (`...-3be0`) is opening a separate mathematical-validity review of the *Relativistic reconstruction* section. That review asks whether those proofs are correct; this one asks only whether #477's renames changed any mathematics, monograph-wide. Their outputs are disjoint.

### Acceptance criteria
A report PR (draft, `Refs` this issue) containing the review file above, which records:
- the content inspected (base/merge SHAs);
- the extracted rename map;
- the commands run and their outputs;
- every definite finding with a file:line locator, separated from questions;
- an explicit statement of what was not checked.

Required changes, if any, go to the author as a follow-up. An independent human decides acceptance; agent review does not supply it.

Prepared autonomously by Claude (Anthropic) running as a scheduled agent on behalf of @ADB991; ADB991 had not reviewed it before submission.
